sites.ownership: The application controller owns the shared single-window lifecycle state.
sites.justification: App actions and activation signals need one mutable slot for the active window and the one-shot session-restore gate.

sites.ownership: GTK tests reuse the shared application-state slot.
sites.justification: The test harness drives the same window lifecycle and restore behavior as the runtime application wiring.

sites.ownership: The test-only window helper borrows the shared app-state slot.
sites.justification: Tests need controlled access to the active-window slot without introducing a second window-lifecycle path.

sites.ownership: App-scoped actions borrow shared application state.
sites.justification: New, open, recent-open, and quit actions must reuse the current window or create one exactly once.

sites.ownership: File actions borrow shared application state.
sites.justification: New, open, open-folder, and recent-open actions need the same active-window slot as the rest of application startup.

sites.ownership: Application utility actions borrow shared application state.
sites.justification: Preferences, help, about, and quit actions must present against the current window or create one through the central window helper.

sites.ownership: Activation and open lifecycle callbacks borrow shared application state.
sites.justification: Lifecycle routing needs the same active-window slot and restore gate as app actions.

sites.ownership: The window-creation helper updates shared application state.
sites.justification: Creating and tearing down the primary window requires one mutable slot to avoid duplicate windows.

sites.ownership: The close coordinator owns the active sequential close queue.
sites.justification: Unsaved tab-close, window-close, and quit flows need mutable queue progress without leaking state into the window shell.

sites.ownership: The search controller owns one mutable binding to the active tab and active search context.
sites.justification: Workspace-level search preserves query state while rebinding highlights, match counts, and replace state to the selected tab.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its mutable document format, live source file, file-monitor, deferred external-change state, and in-flight IO state.

sites.ownership: The window-owned zoom controller owns the resolved base editor font description.
sites.justification: Zoom and font changes need one mutable source of truth that can update all open tabs and the minimap without duplicating state per tab.

sites.ownership: The window-owned zoom controller owns the current zoom percentage for the whole workspace window.
sites.justification: Window-scoped zoom actions must clamp, reset, and reapply the same percentage across every attached editor tab.

sites.ownership: The preferences controller owns the staged editor-preferences state for the dialog lifetime.

sites.ownership: Theme preference wiring borrows the shared staged-state cell.
sites.justification: The theme row must honor the same syncing guard used by the other preferences rows during initialization.

sites.ownership: Toggle preference wiring borrows the shared staged-state cell.
sites.justification: Switch rows need the same shared syncing guard so initial UI population never becomes a settings write.

sites.ownership: Each switch-row helper borrows the shared staged-state cell.
sites.justification: The generic toggle handler must reuse the same local guard state across line numbers, minimap, word wrap, and indentation mode.

sites.ownership: SpinRow setup borrows the shared staged-state cell.
sites.justification: Tab-width and indent-width rows stage edits locally before a commit path writes the sanitized value into GSettings.

sites.ownership: Each spin-row handler keeps a shared handle to the staged-state cell.
sites.justification: The change, activate, and focus-out callbacks must coordinate staged numeric edits through one shared state object.

sites.ownership: Spin-row commit logic borrows the shared staged-state cell.
sites.justification: Commit-time normalization must read the staged dirty flag and temporarily enter syncing mode before updating the row widget.

sites.ownership: Document-format preference wiring borrows the shared staged-state cell.
sites.justification: The line-ending row and format-row synchronization must share the same guard so selected-tab updates do not recursively write back into the active document.

sites.ownership: Document-format row synchronization borrows the shared staged-state cell.
sites.justification: Selected-tab changes need to update encoding and line-ending rows without firing the user-change handlers.

sites.ownership: The dialog-scoped syncing helper mutates the shared preferences state.
sites.justification: Preferences initialization and sanitized write-back need one explicit guard that suppresses recursive signals without weakening GSettings timing rules.

sites.ownership: The staged SpinRow read helper borrows the shared preferences state.
sites.justification: The dialog must be able to query whether a numeric row has staged changes before deciding to commit on focus-out.
